judged_text: The sharing-mode return of refreshOAuthTokens - a raw fetch Response - is assigned to a HubspotToken-typed variable and consumed as a Hubspot token, so every field the following code reads (access_token, expires_in, refresh_token) is undefined. Under credential sync the Hubspot refresh computes a NaN expiry_date and persists a credential with undefined access_token, so every subsequent Hubspot API call fails authentication until the user re-authorizes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is the raw `fetch(...)` Response object. However callers expect a token-shaped object. For Hubspot (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` will receive a `Response` in sharing mode, not a `HubspotToken`, so any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` / `expires_in` (implied by the comment immediately after the call) will be `undefined`, producing incorrect expiry calculations and persisting broken credentials. The same mismatch is visible elsewhere (e.g. Google uses `res?.data` which a fetch `Response` does not have), confirming the defect is real and diff-grounded.
